This approach also ensures the split is as even as possible (the difference between any two shares is at most 1). The existing test passes without modification, fulfilling all constraints in the ticket.

The `to_vec()` method correctly iterates from `tail` for `len` steps, wrapping around as needed, returning elements in chronological order. All public API methods match the required signatures, and the logic holds for any capacity ≥ 1 and multiple wrap-arounds.

The provided `solution.sh` correctly fixes the off-by-one error for inclusive ranges and single-line queries by using `$((end - start + 1))`. A robust solution would use `sed -n "${start},${end}p"` or explicitly validate line counts before printing.
